title: RTU Monthly
instructions:
MAINTENANCE SCHEDULE | HVAC RTU MONTHLY CHECKLIST PREVENTATIVE MAINTENANCE PROGRAM
INSTRUCTIONS monthly
Unit number, serial number, or unique identifier:
: The HVAC RTUs (Roof Top Units) are scheduled for maintenance . Perform checks and cleanliness.
"X"" or slash ( / ) appropriate box when the item is inspected. X for acceptable condition or complete. Slash items that need to be revisited,
create work orders based off the slash marks and complete the X just as you would a room PM."
YEAR
DATE
MAINTENANCE
Turn off the power
 rinse after 5-minutes.
DO NOT LET COIL CLEANER STAY ON COILS FOR LONGER THAN 5 MINUTES
: All power must be turned off prior to performing maintenance on rooftop HVAC units
Replace all air filters, ensuring proper airflow direction. Be sure to date the air filters with a marker
Inspect fans: ensure fans able to spin freely without wobbles or rattling
Inspect belts for wear, replace as needed. Check belt tension, adjust if needed, belts should have 3/4" of "bounce". Do not overtightend
Visually inspect heat exchangers, be watchful for excessive rust buildup
Check economizer: Make sure that dampers, actuators, and temperature sensors are still functioning correctly
Check drainage: Clogged drain pipes can cause damage by not allowing water and other liquids to properly escape the RTU unit
Check electrical section with POWER OFF. Check for loose wiring connections, tighten as needed. Check for blown fuses
Inspect Coil cleanliness and clean as needed. Clean coils on a regular schedule of MARCH, JUNE, and SEPTEMBER at a minimum. DO NOT CLEAN COILS DURING WINTER MONTHS
Utilize water from a garden hose (low pressure), spraying from the inside out. If coils are extremely dirty, use non-acidic coil cleaner and
NOTES

checklist.label: Turn off all power before performing maintenance on rooftop HVAC units.
Replace all air filters, ensuring proper airflow direction. Be sure to date the air filters with a marker
Inspect fans: ensure fans able to spin freely without wobbles or rattling
Inspect belts for wear, replace as needed. Check belt tension, adjust if needed, belts should have 3/4" of "bounce". Do not overtightend
Visually inspect heat exchangers, be watchful for excessive rust buildup
Check economizer: Make sure that dampers, actuators, and temperature sensors are still functioning correctly
Check drainage: Clogged drain pipes can cause damage by not allowing water and other liquids to properly escape the RTU unit
Check electrical section with POWER OFF. Check for loose wiring connections, tighten as needed. Check for blown fuses
Inspect Coil cleanliness and clean as needed. Clean coils on a regular schedule of MARCH, JUNE, and SEPTEMBER at a minimum. DO NOT CLEAN COILS DURING WINTER MONTHS
Clean with low-pressure water from inside out; if needed use non-acidic coil cleaner and rinse after five minutes. Never leave cleaner on coils longer than five minutes.

instructions:

Unit number, serial number, or unique identifier:
: Perform checks and cleanliness.

create work orders based off the slash marks and complete the X just as you would a room PM."
MONTH YEAR
DATE
MAINTENANCE
INDOOR HEAD UNIT
Clean the primary removable mesh filters located underneath the pop-up cover of the head unit
Check and clean the evaporator coil as needed. Do not use acid coil cleaner and do not let sit for more than 5 minutes
Check and clean the blower wheel as needed. Compressed air to blow dust off is sufficient
Check the condensate pan and condensate tubing for clogs, clean out as needed
If a condensate pump is applicable, check the pump for functionality and ensure no clogs/debris
OUTDOOR CONDENSING UNIT
: All power must be turned off prior to performing maintenance on the outdoor condensing unit of the split system

Utilize water from a garden hose on a low pressure setting, clean the coils. If coils are extremely dirty, use non-acidic coil cleaner and

title: 2025 Winter Preparedness Checklist
instructions:
Winter Preparedness Checklist 
10.10.2025 
V1 
Maintenance & IT -> Additional Resources 
Training on where the water shutoffs are and how to shut them off. Photos and drawings/maps posted 
near timeclocks, BOH, and in the emergency manual. 
Make sure all stairwell and vestibule heaters are working properly. 
Make sure there is adequate heat in all back of house areas. Please have maintenance staff check all 
back of house areas daily for cold spots. All BOH areas must be maintained above 40°F. 
Ensure all buildings are “weather tight.” Close all windows, doors, vents, etc., and seal any 
openings in exterior walls, ceilings/roofs, and floors to prevent exposure to outside air. 
Insulating piping and installing heat tracing lines on critical piping will substantially decrease the 
risk of a potential pipe freeze up. Be sure that facilities personnel inspect hard-to-heat areas. 
Verify all roof drains, drainpipes and gutters are free of debris and will provide 
adequate water drainage. Complete Fall Clean Up of all planting beds and planters 
Ensure any extended OOO rooms are checked regularly to ensure adequate heating 
levels are maintained. 
If you have a dry sprinkler system, please make sure that water is drained from low 
points. 
Check Fire Pumps to make sure pump room has adequate heat 
Ensure continuous rooftop exhaust fans are operational 
Ensure automatic louvers systems are functional. For example - Behind commercial dryers, these should 
automatically close when dryers turn off. If not, repair and/or winterize(insulate and cover) 
Make sure fire panel is fully functioning with no troubles. 
Make sure PIC training is conducted with Managers, Front Desk, Auditors, and engineering staff. 
Discuss who is responsible for shoveling/applying ice melt, how often it should be done,etc. 
Flush and winterize outdoor lawn sprinkler system Bring in outdoor furniture if not weather-resistant. 
Have wet floor signs handy, along with doodlebug/spray to clean up dry salt 
Talk to staff about winter safety and planning for more travel time. 
Service and tune up snow blowers to ensure they are working properly. Inspect Shuttle van tires to 
determine if they are in good condition and safe for the winter conditions. 
Ensure Storm Recovery training on is conducted with staff/Emergency response teams. To include: 
inspecting, documenting, and repair to any property damages such as (but not limited to) roofs, 
skylights, and overhangs, notifying ERTs of any injuries or deaths, and supply replenishments for 
preparation of subsequent storms 
Have the following items on hand for guests and staff during winter emergencies 
Ice melt (present at all building entrances) 
Shovels 
Car scrapers 
Flashlights 
Extra blankets 
Cans of deicer 
Dollar store snug gloves for guests who forget 
Portable car battery charger and/or set of jumper cables 
Ensure Snow removal agreements are in place, insurance documents on file. 
Mark curbs/obstacles with flags 
Post snow removal company's number at the front desk along with a log to track 
when they are removing snow and/or salting/sanding lot. 
It is imperative that emergency access roads are cleared. It is important to 
communicate the procedures to be followed during severe weather to key operating 
and emergency personnel.
